title: I or me, he or him
goal: Use subject and object pronouns correctly, even in pairs
intro: Pronouns change their form: I/me, he/him, she/her, we/us, they/them. The first form does the action (subject). The second form receives it or comes after a preposition (object). Mistakes usually happen when there are two people: “me and my friend went” sounds informal and is wrong in careful English.

rules.rule: Subject (before the verb): I, he, she, we, they.
Object (after the verb or a preposition): me, him, her, us, them.
With two people, test each one alone. Put yourself last.
examples: My friend and I went out. (I went out.)
He invited my wife and me. (He invited me.)

mistakes.wrong: Me and my friend went to Goa.
mistakes.right: My friend and I went to Goa.
mistakes.why: Subject: I. And put yourself last.

mistakes.wrong: Between you and I, he is wrong.
mistakes.right: Between you and me, he is wrong.

mistakes.wrong: He told to me that he was busy.
mistakes.right: He told me that he was busy.
mistakes.why: “Tell” takes the person directly: tell me.

mistakes.wrong: Him and his wife are coming.
mistakes.right: He and his wife are coming.

ex.y: Subject: I are twins → my sister and I.

ex.q: Me and Anil are working on this project.
ex.fixed: Anil and I are working on this project.

ex.q: Please send the report to Neha and I.
ex.fixed: Please send the report to Neha and me.

ex.q: Can you share it with she?
ex.fixed: Can you share it with her?

ex.q: Let ___ help you with that bag. (I / me)

ex.a: My wife and I love old films.

ex.q: Correct this: “Me and my brother play cricket on Sundays.”
a: My brother and I play cricket on Sundays

talk: Tell the coach about something you did recently with a friend or family member. Use “my friend and I” and “with him” or “with her”.
